When authors incorporate esoteric concepts into their narratives, it can be a deliberate attempt to add depth and complexity to the story. This approach is often referred to as "esoteric storytelling" or "symbolic storytelling."

  By weaving in esoteric themes, authors may be trying to tap into the collective unconscious, as proposed by Carl Jung, which suggests that certain universal symbols and archetypes are shared across cultures and time. This can create a sense of resonance and familiarity with the audience, making the story more relatable and engaging.

  The Kabbalah, in particular, is a Jewish mystical tradition that explores the nature of the universe and the human condition. Its symbolism and concepts, such as the Sephirot and the Tree of Life, can be used to represent complex ideas and emotions in a way that is both subtle and powerful.

  When authors draw upon esoteric concepts, they may be attempting to:

  • Create a sense of mystery and intrigue, inviting the audience to explore the deeper meanings and symbolism behind the story.
  • Tap into the audience's existing knowledge and experiences, making the story more relatable and personal.
  • Explore complex themes and ideas in a way that is both subtle and powerful, avoiding didacticism and instead allowing the audience to draw their own conclusions.
  • Create a sense of connection to the author's own spiritual or philosophical beliefs, adding a layer of authenticity and depth to the narrative.

  However, it's also possible that authors may simply be intuitively tapping into archetypal structures, which are universal patterns and images that recur across cultures and time. This can be seen in the work of authors like Joseph Campbell, who explored the concept of the "monomyth" – a universal pattern of storytelling that appears across cultures and time.

  Ultimately, the use of esoteric concepts in storytelling is a complex and multifaceted phenomenon that can be interpreted in many different ways. Whether it's a deliberate attempt to add depth and complexity to the narrative or an intuitive tapping into universal patterns and symbols, the result can be a rich and engaging story that resonates with audiences on a deep level.
